Intrepid

/in-TREP-id/ - the stress falls on TREP · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Intrepid means fearless and brave in the face of danger.

Intrepid to the last, the retired smokejumper asked only which ridge needed her.

Worked Example

When the kayaker capsized beyond the breakers, the seventeen-year-old lifeguard swam out through a squall that had emptied the beach — not recklessly, but with the trained, steady nerve the word intrepid was made for.

Intrepid is literally 'not trembling' — in- ('not') + trepidus ('alarmed') — and it needs real danger to earn it. Bold risks embarrassment; daring loves flair; intrepid keeps its nerve where the stakes are genuine.

How Intrepid Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

fearless

fearless: without fear — flat statement, no sense of trial

dauntless

dauntless: impossible to discourage, however long the ordeal

daring

daring: drawn to risk for its flair — the showman's cousin

Antonyms

timid

timid: shrinking from any risk at all

fearful

fearful: ruled by the fear itself

How Strong Is It? — bold → intrepid → foolhardy

bold vs. intrepid

bold vs. intrepid: Bold takes confident risks in daily life and stops short of intrepid, which keeps its nerve in genuine danger.

foolhardy vs. intrepid

foolhardy vs. intrepid: Foolhardy goes further than intrepid — past courage entirely, into ignoring danger that ought to be respected.

Sort It Out

Now place each word on the right side of intrepid.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — in-

Prefix — in-: not

Root — -trepid

Root — -trepid: trembling, alarmed (Latin trepidus)

Put it together

Put it together: The real thing: in- ('not') + trepidus ('trembling, alarmed'). The intrepid explorer is un-trembling — fear noted and set aside. Trepidus also gives trepidation, the flutter of dread itself; intrepid is that flutter, cancelled.

Use the root in a new word: trepidation

Use the root in a new word: trepidation: You met trepidation earlier in this course — the trembling dread she felt at the cliff's edge is exactly what an intrepid diver has set aside.

Root Check

Word Choice

formal / literary

Intrepid carries a whiff of the expedition poster — reserve it for genuine danger met with steady nerve. Daring celebrates flair and risk-taking (a daring menu, a daring dress); bold is confidence anywhere; brave is the plain, warm word. Calling the office coffee run intrepid is a joke, and works as one.
